intro: Armenian political debate centers on constitutional reform and the status of the Declaration of Independence, while the government advances the TRIPP transport project and presents the 2027 state budget. In sports, Armenia prepares for a UEFA Nations League match against Cyprus and athletes compete at world championships.

topics.title: Constitutional reform and Declaration of Independence debated
topics.text: Justice Minister Grigor Minasyan and MP Arman Galyan described the 1990 Declaration of Independence as outdated, while Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan vowed to pass a new constitution at all costs. The government plans to publish the draft constitution in November, with the Parliament Speaker stating it would make Armenian the unamendable sole state language.

topics.title: Government advances TRIPP transport corridor project
topics.text: Prime Minister Pashinyan said preparatory work on the TRIPP infrastructure project has begun and that the government has effectively started implementation. The Armenian ambassador briefed Iranian MPs on the latest route agreements, and Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan highlighted the project at the Manama Dialogue.

topics.title: 2027 state budget projects record revenues and spending
topics.text: The draft budget envisages expenditures of 4.072 trillion drams, with revenues projected at $10 billion. Allocations include nearly 674 billion drams for pensions and 614 billion for defense, while tax revenues rose 14.5% in the first ten months of 2026.

topics.title: Armenia prepares for UEFA Nations League match against Cyprus
topics.text: Ticket sales have opened for the Armenia-Cyprus UEFA Nations League fixture. The Football Federation and the Ministry of Education, Science, Culture and Sport both confirmed availability, while Ararat-Armenia appealed to Armenians in Europe for support.

topics.title: Armenian athletes compete at world championships
topics.text: Weightlifters Rafik Harutyunyan and Martin Poghosyan placed 22nd and 23rd respectively at the World Championships in China. Armenian shooters are set to begin competition at the ISSF World Championship in Qatar, and the women's U17 football team lost to Montenegro in European Championship qualifying.

topics.title: Pension reforms and social protection measures outlined
topics.text: Officials confirmed pensions will increase in 2027, with any changes to the cashback programme only raising benefits. Lawmakers proposed mandatory notification of heirs about deceased citizens' pension savings, and a new vulnerability assessment system was presented.

topics.title: Cultural events mark anniversaries and festivals
topics.text: Meghri concluded its tenure as CIS Cultural Capital, handing the title to Maladzyechna, Belarus. UNESCO events in Paris marked Hrachia Acharian's 150th birth anniversary and the centenary of Republic Square, while Yerevan hosts the third International Flute Festival with world-renowned musicians.
